title: Psi27D topological-invariant hypothesis for 3D Navier-Stokes regularity
description: Research hypothesis: an explicitly defined topological/geometric invariant on a declared manifold Sigma_1766 embedded in R^27 may provide a verifiable bound or control relation for vorticity or velocity-gradient growth in 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes flow.
system_boundary: 3D incompressible Newtonian Navier-Stokes flow with explicitly declared initial conditions, boundary conditions, viscosity and forcing, plus a separately defined candidate manifold/invariant mapping.

candidate_mapping.source_structure: E8-related data may be used as an input structure only after an explicit map is defined.

equations_to_test: partial_t u + (u dot grad)u = -grad(p) + nu Delta u + F
Psi27D = candidate functional of the declared flow and mapping
candidate bound: ||grad u|| <= F_bound(Psi27D, initial_data, nu, boundary_data)
candidate continuation relation: bounded Psi27D -> integral_0^T ||omega(t)||_infinity dt < infinity
assumptions: The 27-dimensional manifold must be explicitly defined rather than inferred from the label alone.
Any E8-to-R^27 relation must be an explicit mathematical construction, not a visual analogy.
The candidate invariant must be dimensionally well-defined.
A bounded numerical trajectory does not constitute a proof of global regularity.
UPI's reduced rigid-vortex field is a control model and is not a substitute for a general 3D Navier-Stokes solver.
null_model: Standard 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes evolution without the proposed Psi27D constraint or invariant.
controls: Manufactured forcing with independently known solution where available
Ablation with the Psi27D term/invariant disabled
test_method: Define Sigma_1766 and the E8-to-manifold map formally.
Perform dimensional and mathematical consistency checks.
Compute Psi27D along independently generated Navier-Stokes trajectories.
Compare Psi27D against ||omega||_infinity, ||grad u||_infinity and the BKM-relevant vorticity integral.
Run resolution, timestep and perturbation convergence tests.
Attempt adversarial counterexamples and ablation tests.
Require independent reproduction before any scientific promotion.
predictions: If the hypothesis is useful, Psi27D should show reproducible bounded/invariant behavior across declared regular-flow controls.
A nontrivial quantitative relationship should emerge between Psi27D and vorticity/gradient growth that survives resolution and timestep refinement.
The proposed control should outperform or add information beyond the null model rather than merely re-encoding existing diagnostics.
falsification_conditions: No well-defined invariant can be constructed from the proposed mapping.
The candidate quantity is dimensionally inconsistent or coordinate-dependent when invariance is required.
Psi27D fails to remain bounded/invariant under controlled regular flows.
Any apparent correlation disappears under resolution, timestep, perturbation or null-model controls.
A counterexample exhibits bounded Psi27D while the relevant regularity-control quantity diverges.
The proposed relation reduces algebraically to an already-known diagnostic without adding a new bound.

evidence.notes: Defines a falsifiable research program only; no mathematical proof or experimental verification is claimed.

status_guard: Do not promote to EST from software tests or numerical simulations alone.
